skill: Constructing and Solving a Dilution Model: Inflow Equals Outflow
learner_operation: Infer nutrient entry cr and mixed outflow rQ/V, form and solve Q′=cr-rQ/V with Q(0)=Q0, then select the matching expression; moderate cases also evaluate at t and round.
reasoning_steps: Constant volume follows from equal positive inflow and outflow.
Multiply concentration by flow for mass entry; divide current amount by volume for concentration at exit.
Solve constant-coefficient first-order linear ODE: Q(t)=cV+(Q0-cV)exp(-rt/V).
Apply initial condition; select one of five mathematical radio options, optionally evaluate and round to two decimals.
response_contract: All ten captured questions use a single five-choice math radio bank. Canonical example lacks answer fields. Easy cases request an expression; moderate cases an evaluated amount.
difficulty: Requested easy: expression identification with small rational/decimal coefficients, fixed volume; no variable-volume or overflow stages.
invariants: Equal positive inflow/outflow r and constant positive V; complete mixing.
Positive incoming concentration: tutorial explicitly contrasts this lesson with clean-water dilution.
Initial mass nonnegative; correct expression must satisfy both ODE and initial value.
Keep expression identification vs numerical evaluation aligned with supported difficulty.
Preserve five-choice radio response and complementary plus constant-particular solution method.
permitted_variations: V, r, concentration, initial mass and contextual nouns may vary consistently.
The sign of Q0-cV is incidental: both increasing and decreasing approaches preserve the method (decreasing numerical source 8f9ca797-1282-5c7a-958a-6e7a8b023c5c).
Eligible correct expression position, distractor coefficients, sign, rate and asymptote assignments may vary; do not always attach correctness to a recognizable bank layout.

Source easy banks include two distinct profiles: incorrect-rate/sign/initial-mass distractors, and common-rate alternatives all satisfying the initial condition. These require distinguishing rate and/or asymptote, not just initial value.
For numeric cases, positive evaluation time may vary; unit/context changes are irrelevant if numeric parameters fixed.
